subject: GCP private offer: utilization forecasting & invoice timing coordination
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@bluepeak.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarifying GCP private offer drawdown and invoice timing

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BluePeak is excited about the performance numbers. Before we sign the private offer, procurement has a couple of questions about how committed credits draw down against usage and when Redwood will issue invoices. Our finance team needs a predictable schedule for recognition and to align with our quarter-close (Q4).

Specifically:
- If we exceed the monthly target in Month 1, how does that affect the remaining committed balance?
- Do you support smoothing (spreading a multi-month commit evenly across calendar months) for invoicing?
- Can you issue invoices at customer-specified dates (e.g., month-end vs. start of month) so our PO matches the billings?

We want to avoid end-of-quarter surprises. I've cc'd procurement@bluepeak.com for PO processing. Can you share any examples or a simple forecast template we can fill out?

Thanks,
Alice
Procurement Lead
BluePeak Analytics
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying GCP private offer drawdown and invoice timing

Alice —

Appreciate the clear questions. Short answers first:
- Drawdown: committed credits are consumed against actual usage first; overage (if any) is billed as additional consumption charges. If you prepay a commit for N tokens/units, usage reduces that pool until depleted.
- Smoothing: yes, we can support an invoicing schedule that smooths the commitment across months for billing/recognition purposes. This is an invoicing alignment — it does not change usage accounting in telemetry.
- Invoice dates: we can align invoice issuance to specific cadence (e.g., last day of month) but we need this to be agreed in the PO and reflected in the DocuSign so finance has matching dates.

I attached a simple forecast template (utilization_forecast_q4.xlsx) and the latest Private Offer terms (Private_Offer_Terms_v3.pdf). Marissa (cc) is our marketplace finance lead and can propose a smoothing plan that preserves Redwood's revenue recognition constraints while giving BluePeak predictable invoicing. Soojin will help with HubSpot/deal-side items.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alice to populate the forecast template with expected monthly run-rate for the committed period.
2) Marissa to propose a billing cadence and any pre-billing options.
3) We exchange a final DocuSign PO that matches the agreed dates.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps — what time zone are you in (I assume PST)?

Best,
David Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@bluepeak.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying GCP private offer drawdown and invoice timing

Hi Alice —

Thanks for raising this. I reviewed the terms and ran the numbers for a couple of smoothing options. Key proposals below (attached is the forecast we used):

Option A — Monthly smoothing (preferred for customer predictability):
- Commit is recognized as an even monthly invoice over the contracted term (e.g., $120k commit -> $10k/mo for 12 months).
- Actual usage will reduce the underlying committed pool; overage billed monthly.
- If committed pool is depleted early, invoices stop for future months (we issue a reconciliation invoice for any overage).

Option B — Front-loaded + true-up (preferred for Redwood cashflow):
- Bill 50% upfront at contract start, remaining 50% split evenly across the next N months.
- True-up at quarter end for usage delta.

Notes:
- We can align invoice issuance to your month-end close (we can set invoice date to last calendar day).
- For recognition and PO matching, DocuSign must show the invoice cadence and PO number.
- Attached: utilization_forecast_q4.xlsx (filled with example numbers) and Private_Offer_Terms_v3.pdf (minor edits in section 4.2 regarding billing cadence).

If you want us to try a specific smoothing run with your forecast numbers, send the filled sheet and Karthik (cc) can run the amortization schedule and produce the actual invoice dates.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Marketplace Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@bluepeak.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluepeak.com
Date: 2026-11-24T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying GCP private offer drawdown and invoice timing

Marissa —

Thanks, this is helpful. We ran the forecast internally and attached our numbers to the sheet (sent in a follow-up email — procurement copy). Our preference is Option A (even monthly smoothing) with invoice dates on the last business day of each month. We also need the first invoice dated Dec 31 so it hits our Q4 accruals correctly.

A couple of asks:
- Can you include language in the DocuSign that states invoices are to be issued on the last business day and that unused committed value is refundable only per the cancellation terms?
- We will provide a PO once we have the DocuSign reflecting those dates.

If you can run the amortization and share the payment schedule, procurement will prepare the PO and routing instructions.

Cheers,
Alice
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@bluepeak.com>, procurement@bluepeak.com
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying GCP private offer drawdown and invoice timing

Alice —

Attached is the amortization schedule per Option A, with invoice dates on the last business day of each month. Summary:
- Total commit: $240,000 over 12 months -> $20,000 invoice each month starting 2026-12-31.
- We will issue invoices with the PO number you provide; invoices will reference the DocuSign agreement id.
- If actual usage in any month > committed monthly allowance, overage will be invoiced the following month as consumption charges.

Next steps:
1) David to send the DocuSign with the updated clause about invoice cadence and PO matching (we've cc'd legal on the language).
2) Alice/procurement to return signed PO via DocuSign.

I've uploaded the schedule and a sample DocuSign template here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCexampleUtilForecast

-Karthik
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

Alice —

Thanks for confirming Option A. I've updated the DocuSign to include the invoice cadence language and the clause about unused committed value tied to cancellation terms. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/samples/rdw-bluepeak-2026 (also attached as docusign-purchase-order.pdf).

Best,
David
